prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across frames 1–2, the table and bowls are about 0.4–0.8 m in front of and below the wearer, while the wearer’s arm is nearer; chairs, bottles, and the rear wall are roughly 1–3 m away. Frame 3 places a person and door immediately in front-right at about 0.3–1 m, with the surrounding room farther away; frame 4 shows a nearby doorway or wall edge on the right and a partially visible person roughly 1–2 m ahead. In frame 5, a silver car occupies the near left/centre at roughly 1–2 m, a red car is farther ahead at about 3–5 m, and people and motorcycles are more distant or partly outside the frame. Brightness makes near surfaces, depth boundaries, occlusion order, and the transition from the indoor table area toward the doorway and outdoor cars clearer than RGB alone, but metric distances are only rough and the black or saturated regions—especially frames 3–5—appear unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates the oven or counter, bowl, person, chairs, bottle, cars, motorcycle, and several partly visible people, clarifying which overlapping pixels belong to distinct instances. In frame 1, a person extends from the lower-right toward a bowl about 0.5 m away, with the bowl above-left of the person’s visible arm; in frame 2, a bottle lies left of two chairs about 1–2 m ahead, while a person is partly occluded by or beside the right chair. Frames 3–4 are dominated by a nearby person-shaped region on the right or centre-right, partly outside the image, indicating close occlusion as the camera turns or passes nearby; frame 5 separates a near silver car on the left from another car and person ahead-right, with a motorcycle clipped at the far-right edge. This map reveals object boundaries and partial occlusions that are difficult to isolate in RGB, but several masks merge with large background regions, some labels are misplaced or truncated, and it provides no dependable metric distance or gaze direction.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only a magenta hand skeleton in frame 1, about 0.5 m in front of the wearer and above the tabletop near the bowls, making the hand’s articulated position clearer than in RGB. No body skeleton is recovered, and frames 2–5 contain no reliable pose despite visible or segmented people, so their facing direction, gaze, limb reach, and turning cannot be determined from this map. Combined with RGB, the detected hand is within the nearby person’s arm reach and may partly overlap the bowl area, while other people and objects remain spatially unconnected by pose landmarks. The map is therefore highly incomplete and unreliable for tracking approach, retreat, orientation, or interpersonal spacing across the five frames.
